title: Finite-stage hypercohomology model for a Cartesian open extension
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], let $p:V\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $i:W\hookrightarrow T$ be an arbitrary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $J$ be an injective module over the constant ring sheaf on $V\times_TW$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Write $k:V\times_TW\hookrightarrow V$ and $F=k_!J$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $Q\to T$ be an affine weakly contractible object of the small pro-etale site [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $P=Q\times_TV$, and let $R$ be the underlying ring sheaf of the constant sheaf $A_P$. Then $P$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. There exist a small filtered category $I$ and a diagram $K:I\to\operatorname{Ch}(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] such that: (i) $K_a^b=0$ for every $a\in I$ and $b<0$; (ii) $H^q(P,K_a)=0$ for every $a\in I$ and integer $q>0$; and (iii) for every integer $q$ there exists an isomorphism $H^q(Q\times_TV,F)\cong H^q(P,\varinjlim_IK)$, where the left side means derived evaluation at the site object $Q\times_TV\to V$, and hypercohomology uses the published ring-sheaf construction [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections].

proof.text:
Put $F=k_!J$. We first record an evaluation identity, valid for any sheaf $G$ on $V$ and any affine weakly contractible object $Q\to T$. Choose a bounded-below injective resolution $G\to I^\bullet$: the small constant-ring module category is Grothendieck with enough injectives by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] supplies a bounded-below injective representative. It computes the ordinary $Rp_*G$ by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Evaluation at $Q$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-wcontractible-affine-evaluation-colimits]. For $P=V\times_TQ$, the morphism $P\to V$ is weakly etale by base-change stability in [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] says that restricting $I^\bullet$ to $P$ remains an injective resolution. The direct-image section formula therefore gives
$$ (R^qp_*G)(Q)=H^q((p_*I^\bullet)(Q))=H^q(I^\bullet(P))=H^q(P,G|_P). $$
This is an identity of module groups, with no appeal to geometric-point stalks. For a proper morphism $h:Y\to Q$ and a sheaf $M$ on $Y$, choose a bounded-below injective resolution $M\to K^\bullet$. The direct-image formula at the terminal object is $(h_*K^\bullet)(Q)=K^\bullet(Y)$. Exact evaluation on $Q_{\mathrm{proet}}$ therefore gives $(R^qh_*M)(Q)=H^q(K^\bullet(Y))=H^q(Y,M)$. Here exact evaluation on $Q_{\mathrm{proet}}$ follows from the slice-site identification in the restriction lemma and the following lifting calculation: $Q$ remains weakly contractible in the slice: a section of a sheaf over the terminal slice object is a map from $h_Q$ over $h_Q$. An epimorphism in that slice is an epimorphism of the underlying sheaves, so weak contractibility lifts this map; the lift is automatically over $h_Q$ because its composite to $h_Q$ is the identity. Thus the exact-evaluation statement applies on $Q_{\mathrm{proet}}$ as well.

proof.text: Fix an affine weakly contractible $Q\to T$, write $Q=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and put $P=V\times_TQ$, $W_Q=W\times_TQ$, $U_Q=U\times_TQ$. Denote the induced maps by $p_Q:P\to Q$, $k_Q:U_Q\hookrightarrow P$, $g:P\to V$ and $g_U:U_Q\to U$. Properness of $p_Q$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], and the open immersions from [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change]. Both $g$ and $g_U$ are weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. Hence $J_Q=J|_{U_Q}$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives].

source.place: Tag 09A5, label section-morphism; morphisms.tex Tag 01W4, label lemma-base-change-proper; weakly etale base-change and restriction input

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction] to the site objects $g:P\to V$ and $g_U:U_Q\to U$. Its clauses (1)–(3) identify the actual inverse images $g^{-1},g_U^{-1}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] with restriction, naturally, and the module pullbacks $g^*,g_U^*$ with restriction as constant-$A$ module sheaves. The square formed by $k,g,k_Q,g_U$ is Cartesian since $U\times_VP=U\times_TQ$. Thus [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change], applied to $J[0]$, identifies $F|_P=(k_!J)|_P$ with $k_{Q!}J_Q$. This is the identification of the actual sheaves: all functors in this comparison are exact inverse image and open extension applied in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 09A5, label section-morphism; the extracted inverse-image/restriction comparison and existing pro-etale open-extension base change

proof.text: Set $S=\{b\in B:D(b)\subseteq W_Q\}$. For a finite subset $E\subseteq S$ put $W_E=\bigcup_{b\in E}D(b)$ and $U_E=P\times_QW_E$. These finite subsets form a small nonempty directed poset: $\varnothing$ is an object and $E\cup E'$ is an upper bound. Since $W_Q$ is the complement of a closed set $V(I)$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$, it equals $\bigcup_{b\in I}D(b)$, so $W_Q=\bigcup_EW_E$ and $U_Q=\bigcup_EU_E$. For any affine open $L\subseteq Q$, $D(b)\cap L=D(b|_L)$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. A finite union of quasi-compact subsets is quasi-compact: take a finite subcover for each subset and then their finite union. Thus the inverse image of $W_E$ in each affine $L$ is quasi-compact. By the affine-preimage definition in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $i_E:W_E\hookrightarrow Q$ is a quasi-compact open immersion.

source.place: Finite principal-open exhaustion from the Zariski definition; schemes.tex Tag 01I3, label lemma-standard-open-affine; algebra.tex Tag 00E8, label lemma-quasi-compact

proof.text: The map $k_E:U_E\hookrightarrow P$ is quasi-compact by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change], and $r_E:U_E\to W_E$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. For the open immersion $a_E:U_E\hookrightarrow U_Q$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies the restricted site and constant ring; [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] therefore makes $J_E=J_Q|_{U_E}$ injective. These are the proper vertical maps, quasi-compact horizontal opens and injective coefficients required at each finite stage. For $E=\varnothing$ the site is empty and its unique module sheaf is zero, which is injective directly from its lifting property.

source.place: Tag 09AE, label definition-extension-zero, and slice-site restriction; geometric base-change stability

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-proetale-open-injective-proper-acyclic] to $B=P$, $D=Q$, $C=U_E$, $E=W_E$, $p=p_Q$, $r=r_E$, and the two quasi-compact open immersions just constructed. Both vertical maps are proper, $p_Qk_E=i_Er_E$, the coefficients are the same finite commutative ring $A$, and $J_E$ is an injective on the small pro-etale site. It gives $R^qp_{Q,*}(k_{E!}J_E)=0$ for every $q>0$. Set $F_E=k_{E!}J_E$. The evaluation identity of Step 1, now with base $Q$ and its terminal object, gives $H^q(P,F_E)=0$ for every $E$ and $q>0$. This uses the pro-etale statement of the cited node, not the etale analogue in Stacks Tag 0F7B.

source.place: Tag 0F7B, label lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, motivates the proper/open injective reduction only; the required pro-etale quasi-compact assertion is the existing DAG obligation lem-sp-proetale-open-injective-proper-acyclic

proof.text:
Write $a_E:U_E\hookrightarrow U_Q$. For $E\subseteq E'$, the open-adjunction counit on $U_{E'}$ gives the transition $a_{E!}J_E\to a_{E'!}J_{E'}$ after extension to $U_Q$. Under the Hom adjunction of [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction], these transitions correspond to restriction of maps from $J_Q$: restrictions from $U_{E^{\prime\prime}}$ to $U_{E^{\prime}}$ and then $U_E$ compose to direct restriction to $U_E$. The adjunction bijection thus proves both the identity and composition laws for the transitions, so they form a diagram. Its cocone to $J_Q$ exhibits
$$ \varinjlim_E a_{E!}J_E\cong J_Q. $$
Indeed, by that adjunction a compatible family of maps $a_{E!}J_E\to N$ is exactly a compatible family $J_Q|_{U_E}\to N|_{U_E}$. It glues uniquely to a map $J_Q\to N$: on an arbitrary object of $U_Q$ use its open cover by inverse images of the $U_E$ and the sheaf gluing axiom; this is a pro-etale covering because its maps are open immersions, and on each affine open the Zariski cover has a finite refinement by affine opens; agreements on overlaps follow by passing to $E\cup E'$. Thus the cocone has the colimit universal property. The small colimits exist by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Applying the left adjoint $k_{Q!}$ preserves this colimit, as follows by applying its Hom adjunction to the colimit universal property. Also $k_{Q!}a_{E!}\cong k_{E!}$, since both have right adjoint $a_E^*k_Q^*=k_E^*$. Consequently
$$ F|_P\cong k_{Q!}J_Q\cong\varinjlim_E F_E. $$
All these maps are the maps induced by the open counits, so this is a colimit of the same coefficient sheaves used in Step 6.

source.place: Tag 09AE, label definition-extension-zero; the open-cover gluing and two adjunction universal-property calculations are written out here

proof.text: Take the diagram of finite-stage sheaves constructed in Step 7, concentrated in degree zero, as K. The lower bound is zero. Step 6 gives its positive hypercohomology vanishing. Properness over affine Q makes P quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Step 7 identifies its colimit with the restricted extension, and the injective-resolution calculation of Step 1 gives the displayed hypercohomology isomorphism in every integer degree. This establishes only the model; no filtered-colimit continuity of hypercohomology is invoked.

proof_origin.place: Steps 2–8, finite principal-open exhaustion and filtered hypercohomology model

lean.statement:
theorem exists_cartesianOpen_finiteStage_hypercohomology_model
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {V T W : Scheme.{u}} (p : V ⟶ T) (i : W ⟶ T)
    [IsProper p] [IsOpenImmersion i]
    (J : proEtaleRingModules (pullback p i)
      (proEtaleConstantRing (pullback p i) A)) [Injective J]
    (Q : T.ProEt) [IsAffine Q.left]
    (hQ : ∀ (F G : Sheaf (ProEt.topology T) (Type (u + 1))) (e : F ⟶ G),
      Epi e → Function.Surjective (e.hom.app (Opposite.op Q))) :
    let P := ((proEtaleBaseChange p).obj Q).left
    let R := (sheafCompose (ProEt.topology P)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj (proEtaleConstantRing P A)
    let U : P.ProEt := ProEt.mk (𝟙 P)
    CompactSpace P ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace P ∧
      ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
        (K : I ⥤ CochainComplex (ringedSiteModules.{u + 1} R) ℤ),
        (∀ (a : I) (b : ℤ), b < 0 → IsZero ((K.obj a).X b)) ∧
        (∀ (a : I) (q : ℕ), 0 < q →
          IsZero ((ProEt.ringHypercohomology P R U (q : ℤ)).obj (K.obj a))) ∧
        (∀ q : ℤ, Nonempty
          (((ProEt.ringHypercohomology V
            ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology V)
              (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u + 1} RingCat.{u + 1})).obj
                (proEtaleConstantRing V A)) ((proEtaleBaseChange p).obj Q) q).obj
              ((CochainComplex.singleFunctor
                (proEtaleRingModules V (proEtaleConstantRing V A)) 0).obj
                  ((sfIntrinsicExtensionByZero (pullback.fst p i) A).obj J))) ≅
            (ProEt.ringHypercohomology P R U q).obj (colimit K)))
